name: Buggy Choke to Side Control
summary: Moving to Side Control after a Buggy Choke requires the top player to clear the bottom player's head-and-arm loop before establishing the next control.
description: Moving to Side Control after a Buggy Choke requires the top player to clear the bottom player's head-and-arm loop before establishing the next control.
overview:
The top player is the choke defender even though this transition calls the moving player its attacker. Changing pins does not itself prove that the choke is gone. Clear the arm-and-leg loop first, and do not lift or slam the partner to escape.

Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg. Avoid lifting, dropping, or twisting the partner's trapped leg to force an escape. Use safe inside frames before the arm-to-leg loop fully closes; do not pull or twist the partner's knee.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

Instructional sources: [Kade and Tye Ruotolo — OG Buggy Choke](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=zixbOyLpoOc); [Jay Rodriguez — three Buggy Choke mistakes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MjKERx4N4mY).

attacker.overview:

Move only through available space after the loop opens; tap if the neck is already enclosed. Establish Side Control only after the head is free. Protect the neck during the loop release, then establish the side pin with hip control, a controlled crossface and balanced chest pressure. Shoulder pressure belongs to the completed head-and-hip connection, not to forcing your head out of a closed choke.

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): Which reach starts the Buggy enclosure from below?
flashcards.answer: Watch for an arm reaching past your head and connecting to the same-side leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Arm past head to their same-side leg

plausible: Hand on your head, their knee low
Arm to knee, your head outside
trap: Knee rises, both hands on your hips

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): Which base supports defense with the partner grounded?
flashcards.answer: Keep a balanced base and avoid using the partner's knee or a lift as the means of escape.

plausible: Raise hips to lift their shoulders
Pull linked shin out, narrow base
trap: Lean over raised thigh, feet close

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): Before their grip closes, how do you interrupt the entry?
flashcards.answer: Use safe inside frames before the arm-to-leg loop fully closes; do not pull or twist the partner's knee.
flashcards.answer_line: Place an inside frame between bodies

plausible: Keep forearm outside linking arm
Chase crossface, ignore leg link
trap: Both hands on hip as their arm links

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): What clearance permits you to rebuild the side pin?
flashcards.answer: Move only through available space after the loop opens; tap if the neck is already enclosed.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and arm outside the choke loop

plausible: Chest already touching their chest
Their hips stop moving for a moment
trap: Chin hidden inside the closed loop

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): After release, which controls stabilize side control?
flashcards.answer: Establish Side Control only after the head is free. Keep the shoulders and hips controlled while moving outside the legs.

plausible: Crossface with the hip free to turn
Hip block, shoulders turn off chest
trap: Chest contact, inside knee still in

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): When should you apply settling chest and shoulder pressure?
flashcards.answer: Use balanced pin pressure after clearance; pressure is not a substitute for opening the neck enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: After neck loop and legs are clear

plausible: Force head out through a closed loop
Before checking their inside knee
trap: Hand open, elbow still hooks leg

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): Who supplies the choking loop in the starting position?
flashcards.answer: The bottom player joins an arm and same-side leg around the top player's head and one arm.

plausible: Top player's arm to bottom leg
Bottom linking only the top's limbs
trap: Top player linking own knee to elbow

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): Why can chest-to-chest contact coexist with danger?
flashcards.answer: Existing pin contact does not establish release; check the actual arm-leg enclosure.
flashcards.answer_line: Bottom loop can still hold head/arm

plausible: Chest pin forces elbow off knee
Flat shoulder prevents arm-leg link

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): Your neck is secured despite stable top balance. What next?
flashcards.answer: If the choke is securely established, stable top balance does not justify forcing an escape.
flashcards.answer_line: Tap and have the whole loop released

plausible: Hold pin until their grip fatigues
Open hand clasp, leave leg hooked
trap: Circle knees around the fixed head

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (top): After clearance, what stops a fresh knee returning inside?
flashcards.answer: The completed side pin combines upper-body attachment with a hip block that limits knee reinsertion.
flashcards.answer_line: Hip control with an upper-body pin

plausible: Distant ankle grip, hip unblocked
Crossface alone, near hip unblocked
trap: Chest pressure, hips out of reach

defender.name: Buggy Choke to Side Control Defender
defender.description: Buggy Choke to Side Control (defender): Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
defender.overview:
The top player is the choke defender even though this transition calls the moving player its attacker. Changing pins does not itself prove that the choke is gone. Clear the arm-and-leg loop first, and do not lift or slam the partner to escape.

Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg. Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg. Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.

Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee. Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost. Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

Move through available space with a stable base. Stop and release any trapped neck, shoulder or knee before changing direction; do not force a roll or stack to preserve the route.

If the Buggy connection opens, use a framed hip escape to return the knee for guard retention. Keep the near elbow connected as the opponent settles; reaching back for the lost foot grip leaves the side pin space open.
key_principles: Build the angle: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
Enclose head and arm: Check that the loop contains the necessary upper-body configuration rather than merely hugging your leg.
Keep elbow near knee: Shorten the connection through body position, not by pulling the foot hard toward the face.
Use the torso connection: Close space with the arm, leg, and torso while avoiding twisting force on your own knee.
Recover guard when space opens: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
Release if lifted: Let go when the partner begins lifting you from the mat; do not hang from the choke or invite a slam.

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (bottom): Which frames help you turn onto your side for the entry?
flashcards.answer: Use safe shoulder and hip frames to turn partly onto the side before reaching for the leg.
flashcards.answer_line: Frames at the shoulder and hip

plausible: Arms outside shoulders, back flat
Hands low on hip, shoulders pinned
trap: Hands on linking leg before framing

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (bottom): Why is hugging your thigh alone insufficient?
flashcards.answer: The effective loop contains the opponent's head and one arm rather than only your own thigh.
flashcards.answer_line: Head and arm must also be enclosed

plausible: Their head out, one arm enclosed
Their head in, both shoulders out
trap: Only their wrist over your thigh

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (bottom): What should stay close as you link arm and leg?
flashcards.answer: Elbow-knee proximity comes from body angle; do not manufacture it by pulling the foot against a fixed knee.

plausible: Elbow and hip, knee still distant
Hand and shin, elbow flared away

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (bottom): Which action uses your torso to close the loop?
flashcards.answer: Shortening shoulder-to-hip distance closes space in the head-and-arm enclosure without wrenching the foot.
flashcards.answer_line: Draw shoulder down toward your hip

plausible: Arch the shoulder away from the hip
Lift shoulder, keeping the hip low
trap: Move hips away, keep shoulder high

flashcards.question: Buggy Choke to Side Control (bottom): When the grip fails, how do you resist the new pin?
flashcards.answer: Use a disengaging opponent's movement to insert frames and knees if the choke is lost.
flashcards.answer_line: Frame, shift hips, return a knee

plausible: Reach for old foot with both hands
Flare near elbow behind your head
trap: Shrimp away, leave near knee outside
